transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Alejandro Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Head of ML, Sevanta), Tom Becker (CTO), Liu Zhang (Infra)

Summary: quick scoping call to align success criteria for a 4-week POC exploring hosting options (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem), define benchmarks (latency, throughput, cost), and confirm timeline and deliverables. Customer emphasized data residency and auditability needs plus a firm go/no-go at the end of the pilot.

Topics: success metrics, workload sizing, benchmark plan, networking constraints, security compliance, timeline and next steps.

Timestamps and transcript (note: auto-transcription imperfect; some product names and acronyms may be transcribed slightly off):

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. Quick intros, then we want to nail down what makes the pilot successful for you.

[00:18] Priya: Hi yes thanks. Priya here. We're trying to validate whether we can meet p95 latency under real loads and keep unit cost within our target. Also, we need to prove that no sensitive data leaves our region for the private option.

[00:35] Tom: I just want to add, from infra side, we need guidance on expected network egress and how the KV catch, sorry, K-V cache, behaves with our tokenization patterns.

[00:50] Alejandro: Sure, good point. For context, Redwood's options are Hosted API (fast start), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC or on-prem). Each has different trade-offs on latency, cost predictability, and control.

[01:12] Liu: Quick question — can Dedicated run inside our VPC? We want to avoid NAT egress to other regions.

[01:22] Maya: Dedicated can be deployed as a private-dedicated VPC peering setup for enterprise customers — it depends on contract and the Dedicated flavor. We'll share the network diagram.

[01:40] Priya: For success criteria — list from our side: p95 latency < 200ms for single-turn generation at our median prompt length (~320 tokens), throughput 120-150 RPS for batch inference peak, and cost target under $0.025 per 1k tokens. Plus SOC2 and audit logs, SSO via SAML.

[02:05] Alejandro: That's helpful. From the bench perspective I'd break it down: latency SLOs (cold vs warm), throughput under sustained load, memory/kv cache hit-rate impact, and model quality stability. Also quantify tokenization variability.

[02:30] Tom: How does caching impact Hosted vs Dedicated? My concern is caching warmup after rollouts.

[02:39] Alejandro: Good question. Hosted has global caching heuristics and prefix caching across customers in some cases (we'll confirm privacy boundary) — which speeds up common prompts but less deterministic for strict data residency. Dedicated gives you dedicated KV cache within your pool so warmup times are predictable. Private obviously gives you total control but requires initial warmup and more ops overhead.

[03:05] Priya: So for bench plan, we need reproducible runs. Can Redwood supply a harness or a script we can run inside our infra to simulate the load?

[03:15] Maya: Yes, we can provide a harness. Alejandro will run an internal sim that emulates your 3 workload patterns and share config files so you can reproduce.

[03:28] Alejandro: I'll run a 1k-query throughput sim that mirrors your token distribution and concurrency. I'll also capture tail latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and cache hit stats. Expect raw logs.

[03:42] Liu: Network — we need to validate MTU and TLS passthrough; also whether Redwood uses private peering or inter-region hops for Hosted.

[03:54] Maya: We'll include network topology notes. Hosted uses regional endpoints; sometimes traffic routes through our edge. For strict data residency, Private is the only guaranteed model where customer data never hits Redwood-hosted multi-tenant storage.

[04:12] Tom: Security questions — do you support KMS integration and customer-managed keys for model artifacts and logs?

[04:20] Maya: Yes, in Private we support customer KMS/HSM. In Dedicated we can enable customer-managed keys for stored assets depending on the contract. Hosted supports encrypted-at-rest with Redwood-managed keys; we can discuss bring-your-own-key options for enterprise tiers.

[04:37] Priya: Compliance wise we need audit logs that show request id, user id, model version, and whether a rollout fallback occurred.

[04:46] Alejandro: We can surface token-level traces, model version info, and fallback events in the Console. We'll export a sample audit log format.

[05:05] Priya: For the POC, timeline expectations? We have a board review in 5 weeks and want a go/no-go decision 4 weeks from now. Can Redwood hit that?

[05:18] Maya: We can do a 4-week pilot. Week 0: onboarding and infra checks; Week 1: baseline hosted tests; Week 2: Dedicated sizing + sim; Week 3: Private test (if chosen) and final report; Week 4: decision and recommendations. Does that align?

[05:35] Priya: Yes, as long as the ops time required on our side in Week 0 is reasonable — we can dedicate 2 infra engineers and 1 ML engineer.

[05:45] Liu: We'll need step-by-step VPC peering playbook; don't assume our infra is standard.

[05:52] Maya: We'll send a checklist with required firewall ports, sample Terraform snippets, and a runbook.

[06:05] Tom: Bench specifics — can we run a comparative test: Hosted vs Dedicated equivalent sizing vs Private on similar infra? I.e., apples-to-apples for cost and latency.

[06:18] Alejandro: We can approximate apples-to-apples. For Dedicated I'll size an instance class and run same model/config. For Private the variance depends on your GPU type and network. We'll provide normalized metrics: per-token cost, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and throughput per GPU.

[06:36] Priya: What about model variants and quantization? We rely on a quantized 4-bit config for cost — do you support that in Dedicated/Private?

[06:45] Alejandro: Yes, our runtime supports quantized execution paths. Some kernels differ by hardware; we'll list supported quant levels per instance type. Hosted often exposes the most variants quickly, Dedicated supports stable quant profiles, Private depends on the exact hardware and CUDA/cuDNN versions.

[07:03] Tom: Any gotchas for burst traffic? We have irregular peaks during end-of-day processing.

[07:10] Maya: Dedicated has autoscaling and burst capacity options; Hosted has elastic capacity but less predictable unit cost at scale; Private needs your autoscaler to be configured. We'll model a burst scenario in the sim.

[07:28] Priya: On cost targets, our procurement will consider not just per-token but operational overhead. Can you provide an estimated TCO for each mode across a 12-month forecast?

[07:41] Maya: We'll produce a simple TCO sheet factoring reserved capacity pricing, expected token volumes (you gave a 30M token/month estimate), ops headcount, and expected latency SLO penalties.

[07:58] Liu: A small nit — do you support IP allowlisting for Hosted endpoints? We might lock to customer egress IPs.

[08:05] Alejandro: We support allowlisting and per-token routing policies in certain enterprise tiers; we'll confirm the Hosted options available to Sevanta.

[08:18] Priya: Can we get a sample audit export and a sample SLA?

[08:24] Maya: Yes, I'll share SOC2 summary and a sample SLA. For Hosted we have standard terms; Dedicated comes with a stronger SLA on latency and uptime.

[08:37] Tom: For acceptance criteria at the end of the pilot — propose: 1) meets p95 latency target in chosen mode, 2) throughput meets 80% of peak projected, 3) data residency & auditability validated, and 4) cost within 10% of our target.

[08:58] Priya: That sounds right. Also want a small quality regression check — ensure new model quantization doesn't drop our evaluator score more than 2%.

[09:10] Alejandro: We'll include a basic eval harness and run a diff against your baseline to capture any quality regression. You'll need to provide the eval set.

[09:24] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps quickly — Alejandro will run the sim and share results; Maya to send cost matrix, runbook, sample audit logs, SOC2 summary; Sevanta provides workloads and eval set. Then we schedule the deep-dive network session on Wed next week.

[09:43] Priya: Yep, we'll get the artifacts up by Monday EOD.

[09:50] Tom: Any blockers on Redwood's side to meet the 4-week timeline?

[09:56] Alejandro: No blockers. We may need a short permit for Dedicated pool booking if you want reserved capacity — we'll flag that early.

[10:08] Maya: I'll open a pilot ticket and include the required contacts and timeline.

[10:16] Liu: One more small thing — can Redwood log request trace IDs in our preferred format? We use a proprietary correlation id.

[10:25] Alejandro: We can include a correlation id as an optional header and echo it back in logs. I'll note that as an action item.

[10:36] Priya: Great. If we prove Dedicated meets the metrics, we'll likely move there for predictable costs and isolation. If not, Private remains an option if procurement approves the infra spend. Hosted is our fallback for speed to market.

[10:55] Maya: Perfect. We'll follow up with the artifact bundle by tomorrow and set up the network deep-dive invite.

[11:05] Tom: Thanks all.

[11:08] Meeting ends.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Customer strongly values predictable p95 latency and data residency; Dedicated is their likely preference if pricing and KV cache warmup meet SLAs.
- Sequences of action: Redwood runs sim -> customer runs replay with provided harness -> joint analysis -> final recommendation.

Recap of explicit next steps (also in metadata):
1) Redwood: send pricing matrix, Dedicated sizing guidance, sample SLA and SOC2 summary (owner: Maya Chen; due: 2026-09-17)
2) Redwood SE: run 1k-query throughput sim and share raw logs + summary (owner: Alejandro Ruiz; due: 2026-09-22)
3) Sevanta: upload 3 workload samples + eval set + PII checklist (owner: Priya Nair; due: 2026-09-20)
4) Schedule technical deep-dive for network/VPC routing (target date: 2026-09-22)

References mentioned: cost/latency spreadsheet (to be shared), runbook + Terraform snippets (to be shared), sample audit log export (to be shared).
